President Trump was in Florida Friday campaigning ahead of the November midterm elections for
Republican candidates. Florida has been a reliably red state, but polling shows Democrats
drawing close in several major state races. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis was with Trump,
and he told reporters that Florida will still deliver for the party.
They've got a big crowd in Fort Myers. I know a lot of people are excited.
We've got a lot of races going on, and I think we're going to do very well in Florida,
as we have in recent years.
The U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals has ruled that immigration detainees can be held
in jail without bond pending deportation hearings. Houston Public Media's Andrew Schneider says
the ruling in favor of the Trump administration is all but certain to be appealed to the U.S.
Supreme Court. The Trump administration had argued that undocumented immigrants,
even those who had been in the U.S. for years and had no criminal records,
have no right to a bond hearing as to whether they represent a danger or a flight risk.
The full bench of the Fifth Circuit agreed, reversing a lower court ruling.
Josh Blackmon teaches constitutional law at South Texas College of Law, Houston.
So at least for now, for those people who are being detained in Texas, Mississippi, and Louisiana,
there's no right to a hearing. This case would like to be appealed to the Supreme Court very,
very, very soon.
With the exception of the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, most other circuit courts have ruled
against the Trump administration on this question. For NPR News, I'm Andrew Schneider in Houston.
The editor-in-chief of one of Egypt's widely recognized independent news websites
has been charged with operating an unlicensed media outlet. As NPR's Aya Batrawi reports,
this comes as part of a larger suppression of press freedoms in Egypt.
The independent English and Arabic news outlet Meda Masra says its editor-in-chief Lina Atallah
is being charged with establishing, managing, and operating a website without a license.
The Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights says Atallah will be tried by state prosecutors after
she was released on bail Thursday following more than six hours of questioning.
Meda Masra says it legally challenged the state's rejection of its request for a license in 2022,
and that its request for a license has been pending since 2023.
Atallah is the recipient of multiple international journalism awards. Amnesty International says her
case reflects a wider crackdown following the arrest this month of six journalists from the
Egyptian fact-checking website that said Dutch. Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
A multi-story building in Kenya has collapsed in a busy commercial area of that country's capital.
Officials say many people could be buried underneath the rubble. The building was under
construction when it collapsed along a street which is often crowded with thousands of traders
and residents. Police say they fired tear gas at people they say were looting nearby shops.
You're listening to NPR News.
Kenya's Health Ministry says a second person has now died in that country from Ebola.
The 65-year-old woman was a close relative of the first person to have died on October 5.
She began showing symptoms after being placed in quarantine in Nairobi. Seven other Ebola
patients are still receiving treatment and no new infections have been reported.
New research shows nearly nine in 10 young adults have used artificial intelligence,
but an overwhelming majority don't trust the companies behind it. NPR's Windsor Johnston reports.
New data from Northeastern University reveals sharp differences in how much Americans of different
ages trust artificial intelligence. Researcher David Lazar says the findings highlight a striking
contradiction among those most likely to use the technology. For anxiety, the young people are
clearly the most anxious and of course what's interesting is that they use chat GPT at very
high rates, right? There's a very strong reverse age gradient for using AI, which is younger people
use AI far more than older people. The study also found younger and older Americans favor more AI
regulation. Those in the middle age groups tend to be more optimistic and less supportive of
government oversight. Windsor Johnston, NPR News. The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders now have union
representation. The NFL franchise has agreed to recognize the Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders association
as their collective bargaining agent. The squad has been fighting for years for pay increases.
Forbes magazine has labeled the team as the most valuable pro sports team in the world.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from Rosetta Stone,

More information at RosettaStone.com.
